We need to determine appropriate criminal charge(s) based on facts.

Facts: Sun (male) drunk, angry, broke into Zhang's house (trespassed) and destroyed property: TV, audio, clothes, some burned. Also assaulted Zhang (punched his face). Value 1580 yuan. Later threatened via message to jump into his house? Actually "要跳到其家中" maybe means "to jump into his house"? Not clear. He threatened. Then they settled, compensation, victim forgave.

Potential charges: "故意毁坏财物" (intentional damage to property). Also "故意伤害" (intentional injury) for punching face. Also "非法侵入住宅" (illegal intrusion). In examples, they sometimes include multiple charges: e.g., "故意伤害;故意毁坏财物". For trespass, they used "非法侵入住宅" in one example (the case of breaking into house). That case: 2009-11-17, breaking window, entering bedroom, stealing cash and phone. They labeled "非法侵入住宅". So here he also entered without permission. So could be "非法侵入住宅". However the main acts: damage property and assault. The examples often combine both: e.g., "故意伤害;故意毁坏财物". In the case of assault and property damage, they used both. For example, the case with "故意伤害;故意毁坏财物" (the one with Chen case). That had assault causing heavy injury and property damage. So likely we need both.

Thus answer: [罪名]故意伤害;故意毁坏财物<eoa>

Check if need "非法侵入住宅". Not always included. In that case, they used "非法侵入住宅" when the primary crime was burglary (theft). Here no theft, just damage. The trespass may be considered part of the damage. Might not be listed separately. The examples show they sometimes include "非法侵入住宅" as a charge when there is no theft but intrusion. But not sure. The safe answer: include both "故意伤害" and "故意毁坏财物". That matches pattern.

Thus final answer.
